subject: Fixed advance billing schedule and reconciliation runbook
messages:
From: Maeve Lewis <maeve@heliosai.com>

Cc: procurements@heliosai.com
Date: 2027-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Advance billing schedule / VAT details

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the contract — we're ready to move to the committed prepay but need a clear billing cadence and VAT evidence before procurement signs the first invoice. Can you confirm: 

- The proposed invoicing cadence for the fixed advance (monthly vs quarterly).
- Whether Redwood will issue a VAT invoice or if Helios should self-account (we're UK-registered).
- What supporting docs you can supply (SOC2, VAT proof, bank wiring instructions) for our vendor intake.

Procurement would like to see a one-page schedule and a short reconciliation runbook showing how drawdowns are tracked against the commitment. Can you attach a sample schedule?

Maeve
Procurement Lead, Helios AI
maeve@heliosai.com
From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Maeve Lewis <maeve@heliosai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Advance billing schedule / VAT details

Hi Maeve — thanks for the note. I attached a draft schedule (Advance_Schedule_v1.xlsx) and a short runbook below. Quick answers up front:

- Invoicing cadence: Redwood typically issues the fixed-advance invoice as a single upfront invoice that is then drawn down monthly against committed spend. For Helios we can: (A) single upfront invoice for the full committed amount with monthly drawdown windows (preferred for enterprise accounting), or (B) quarterly prepaid invoices if you prefer smoothing. 

- VAT: Redwood will issue a VAT invoice from Redwood Inference, Inc. (US entity) for the advance. For UK accounts we include the VAT line where applicable; for reverse-charge we can provide a zero-rated invoice plus VAT evidence. We will need Helios' VAT registration number and billing address to populate the invoice header.

- Supporting docs: SOC 2 report, VAT_Proof_UK.pdf (placeholder), and bank wiring instructions are available. DocuSign link for the SOW can be provided as well.

Suggested runbook (summary):
1) Issue upfront advance invoice for committed amount (Invoice triggers: signed SOW + PO).
2) Finance posts invoice and notifies Helios of invoice number + payment due.
3) Upon payment, funds are posted to the Advance Ledger and a monthly drawdown statement is produced on the 1st of each month.
4) Drawdown window: consumption offsets against the ledger daily; once monthly reconciliation closes we produce a drawdown summary and remaining balance.
5) Overage handling: monthly invoice for usage above committed amount.

If that fits, I'll loop in our contracts team and ops to confirm GL codes and the first invoice date.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Maeve Lewis <maeve@heliosai.com>

Date: 2027-04-13T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Advance billing schedule / VAT details

Maeve / Tessa — quick tax ops questions to make the invoice final: 

1) Is Helios VAT-registered in the UK only, or also in any EU countries? If UK-only, we can apply reverse-charge (zero on Redwood invoice) but need Helios VAT number for our records.
2) Billing entity: confirm legal name and exact invoice header (inc. billing address) — will use this on the advance invoice.
3) Do you require separate invoice lines for committed credit vs usage (we usually separate to make reconciliation simpler for customers).
4) For GL mapping: Helios' AP prefers a single PO reference per invoice. If you can provide PO number we will include it in the invoice and the drawdown reports.

Operational note: we will produce a monthly drawdown CSV (format in sheet 2 of the attached) with: invoice_number, period_start, period_end, committed_drawn, usage, remaining_balance. Please confirm the CSV layout is acceptable — I can alter columns if your AP system ingests differently.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Finance Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Maeve Lewis <maeve@heliosai.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Advance billing schedule / VAT details

Hi Karthik / Tessa — thanks. Answers below: 

1) Helios is UK VAT-registered only (GB123456789). Reverse-charge is our preferred approach.
2) Invoice header: Helios AI Ltd, 88 Bishopsgate, London, EC2M 4XD, United Kingdom. PO: HLYS-PO-88921 (please include on all invoices).
3) Separate invoice lines for committed credit and overage is helpful for our accounting system.

I've attached the signed SOW (Signed_SOW_HeliosAI.pdf) and our standard vendor form (procurements@heliosai.com). Bank details will be shared by AP for the wire instructions once invoice is issued.

Please proceed with the draft invoice and we will run it through AP for payment on receipt.

Maeve

Looping in ops notes and a short reconciliation checklist. Tessa — below is the reconciliation runbook we will follow once payment clears: 

Reconciliation runbook (short):
- Step 0: Confirm payment receipt against Invoice HLYS-2027-INV-001 (finance posts to Advance Ledger).
- Step 1: Create Advance Ledger entry (entity: Redwood Inference, ledger_code: ADV-HELYS-01).
- Step 2: Produce monthly drawdown CSV on the 1st (columns: invoice_number, period_start, period_end, committed_drawn, usage, overage, remaining_balance, PO_ref).
- Step 3: Reconcile usage export to the drawdown CSV within 3 business days of month close. Discrepancies > $500 escalate to Finance Ops.
- Step 4: Issue monthly statement to customer with remaining balance and overage charges (if any).
- Step 5: Year-end: produce an annual reconciliation and return any unused committed credit if contract requires.

Action items for Helios: confirm PO HLYS-PO-88921 and preferred CSV column order (we default to the order above). Attached VAT evidence template (VAT_Proof_UK.pdf) — please confirm the number and we will apply reverse-charge.

Priyom Das
Billing Operations | Redwood Inference
